title: 38-34_United Academics v. University of Vermont
text:
VERMONT LABOR RELATIONS BOARD
GRIEVANCE OF )
UNITED ACADEMICS ) Docket No. 24-47
DECISION AND ORDER ON MOTION TO DISMISS
Introduction
The University of Vermont, (“UVM” “University”), has filed with the Vermont Labor
Relations Board (“Board”) a motion to dismiss the Grievance filed on behalf of United
Academics (“Grievant” “Union”) asserting the Board has no jurisdiction to hear the grievance
because Grievant has failed to allege an injury in fact.
On 12/20/24, United Academics filed a Grievance alleging the University violated Article
20.1 of the parties’ Full Time Collective Bargaining Agreement.
Article 20.1 (a) of the CBA addresses the provision of medical insurance and provides
that members seeking to waive insurance coverage, must demonstrate coverage is available to
them under a non-University plan, and “[i]f the faculty member waived coverage for one year,
the waiver will not automatically renew in the subsequent year.”
On October 28, 2024, the University emailed faculty and staff the following:
Starting this year, UVM is moving to an Active Open Enrollment process for
benefit elections, including medical insurance. This means all employees must
actively elect or waive coverage during Open Enrollment to receive benefits for
the upcoming year. While this may be a new practice for some, it ensures
everyone reviews and can select the benefits that best meet their evolving needs.
. . . .
If you do not make an election during Open Enrollment for any of these benefits,
you will not be enrolled for coverage for 2025.
Grievance and Opposition to Motion to Dismiss Exhibit 1 (emphasis in original).
34

DECISION
The University has filed a motion to dismiss asserting the Union failed to state any claim
upon which relief can be granted because there is no actual controversy between the parties, and
therefore, the board lacks jurisdiction. The University maintains the Union has failed to allege
that any faculty was injured in fact by the actual enrollment process, and therefore, it has failed
to allege an actual controversy between the parties.
The jurisdiction of the Board in grievance proceedings is limited by the requirement that
there be an "actual controversy" between the parties. Grievance of Doheny, 34 VLRB 244, 246
(2018) (citing In re Friel, 141 Vt. 505, 506 (1982)). “To satisfy the actual controversy
requirement, there must be an injury in fact to a protected legal interest or a threat of an injury in
fact.” Doheny, 34 VLRB at 246 (internal citations and quotations omitted). Where future harm
is at issue, the existence of an actual controversy turns on whether the employee is suffering the
threat of actual injury to a protected legal interest or is merely speculating about the impact of
some generalized grievance.” Grievance of Boocock, 150 Vt. 422, 424 (1988) (internal
quotations omitted); Grievance of Moriarty, 150 Vt. 160, 164 (1991).
The Union claims Article 20.1 of the CBA mandates that medical insurance for eligible
faculty “begins on the first day of employment” provided that the application is timely submitted
to human resources. Article 20.1. The Union asserts that the Article does not impose a
requirement for faculty to resubmit their application to maintain their health insurance. Instead, it
provides that “if a faculty member waives medical coverage the waiver will not automatically
renew in the subsequent year.” The University, the Union alleges, has altered the process
outlined in Article 20.1, and converted the status quo or default from coverage to waiver and
imposed the burden of renewal of coverage on the faculty member.
35

The University alleges because no member was harmed by its changes in the Fall 2024
open enrollment period, the Grievance is moot. It claims that the Union has failed to assert that
any member has suffered financial harm or been injured by the new policy. The University,
however, has notified faculty of the new policy “starting this year.” The language chosen by the
University suggests that the change will continue in the succeeding years. There remains a threat
of actual injury to a protected legal interest. That no member suffered the loss of their insurance
benefit this year does not minimize or eliminate the risk of such a gap in coverage the next open
enrollment period.
The Vermont Labor Relations Board seeks to resolve an issue on the merits, unless the
Board Rules of Practice or the Collective Bargaining Agreement require it to be dismissed on
procedural grounds. See Grievance of Adam Mickel, 33 VLRB 282, (2016) (citing Grievance of
Monti,10 VLRB 246 (1987)).
At this stage in the litigation, because there remains a future risk or threat of harm to unit
members, the Board will not dismiss the Grievance.
36

ORDER
For the reasons stated above, the motion to dismiss filed by the University is DENIED.
Dated this 23rd day of June 2025, at Montpelier, Vermont.
VERMONT LABOR RELATIONS BOARD
/s/ Robert Greemore
